title: 5 Secrets of Elite Natural Lifters
summary: Based on watching his Noble Natty peers (GVS, Bald Omni-Man, Alex Leonidas), NH lists five mindset secrets of elite naturals: openness to criticism and big goals, owning their progression, treating injuries as their own fault and a chance to improve, ignoring social media comparison, and keeping whatever works instead of chasing 'optimal'. The only thing they have on you is time: train hard for 10 years before judging your genetics.
claims: Copy the mindset of elite naturals, not their methods, which may not fit your body or lifestyle
Elite naturals stay open to learning and criticism; when criticised you can get upset or improve, and they improve
When he critiqued their physiques in his lifter-profile series, none of them got offended; several agreed and asked for advice
Ego carries you forward, but if ego prevents you from fixing mistakes, you stop progressing
People stall when they decide they can't progress any more; elite naturals stay hungry despite physiques 99% would kill for
Be 'delusional' about goals: self-styled realists settle for mediocre goals, while elites aim for godlike goals and say them out loud
Elites progress at the same rate as you; the difference is they don't quit when it slows
Treat slow progress as something you did, not something done to you; blaming genetics is a loser's mindset, even if owning it is delusional
Fast novice gains reach maybe 50-60% of your potential; the other half comes slowly, and most give up on it
Always win: take victories wherever they are (a rep PR, a forearm isolation PR), so no session is a bad session
Injuries don't 'just happen': every injury comes from load mismanagement, fatigue mismanagement or a rep you knew was a bad idea
Control your program's parameters and injuries largely disappear; he went from 'Mr Injury' (ribs, knee, lower back, shoulders) to just elbow tendinitis, which he fixed by changing parameters
GVS hurt his leg chasing a four-plate squat without proper training, then made the best quad gains of his life by adjusting his training
Alex Leonidas hurt his back on a four-plate good morning, built a spinal-stretching regimen and is back to good mornings with 300 lb
Bald Omni-Man hurt his lower back squatting and reworked his program parameters to become bigger and healthier
Injuries are self-imposed shortcomings; only quitting or an injury bad enough to stop training can end your journey
Elite lifters are healthily self-centred; social media shatters the self by having you live through others
Content you consume, including his, should improve your life; if it makes you worse, stop
Jealousy and envy are the original sins of fitness; the system pushes creators to fight for attention
Comparison is the thief of joy; despite a very good body he has at times been unable to enjoy it because of comparison
No one on social media is your competition; you are your own competition
If a method works, keep it; don't change because a YouTuber with a million subscribers says otherwise, but watch for the day it stops working
Obsessing over optimal training is a paradox that leads to a poor physique; optimal is whatever you've proven works on your own body
The only thing elite naturals have on you is time; 3 years versus 15 years of training is the difference between heaven and hell
Train hard for 10 years before talking about your genetics; 99.9% of people on fitness YouTube haven't
Becoming elite is a matter of decision and then application
